newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Senegal's Diouf starts state visit to Ivory Coast.
newsitem.headline: Senegal's Diouf starts state visit to Ivory Coast.

text.p: Senegal's President Abdou Diouf arrived in Ivory Coast on Monday for a four-day state visit aimed at broadening bilateral cooperation, officilas said.
Diouf was greeted at Abidjan aiport by Ivorian President Henri Konan Bedie, who is due to host a first round of bilateral talks on Tuesday.
The two former French colonies have the distinction of being the only countries in West Africa where soldiers have not intervened in government since independence in the early 1960s.

Both heads of state took over from reverred independence presidents. Diouf succeeded Leopold Sedar Senghor who retired from office in 1980. Bedie took over from Felix Houphouet-Boigny who died in 1993 after more than 30 years at the helm.

Ivory Coast under Bedie is championing closer integration of the seven former French West African colonies grouped under the UEMOA monetary union, which now includes Portuguese-speaking Guinea-Bissau.

Ivory Coast and Senegal are the two leading economies of the bloc, which shares a common currency -- the French-backed CFA franc -- and a single central bank based in the Senegalese capital Dakar. Both are members of the larger 16-nation Economic Community of West African States.
